chrysanthemum: The gold-flower, marigold, also called heliochryson, Plin. 21, 25, 96, § 168.—Access. form , Verg. Cul. 403 Sillig.
chrysas: A river of Sicily, now Dittaino, near which is St. Asaro, Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 44, § 96 Zumpt; Sil. 14, 229.
chryselectrum: Gold-colored amber, a precious stone, Plin. 37, 3, 12, § 51.
A dark-yellow precious stone, perh. amber-colored hyacinth, Plin. 37, 9, 43, § 127.
chrysendetus: Set in gold, inlaid with gold: lances,Mart. 14, 97 inscr.—Also absol.: chrȳs-endĕta, ōrum, n. (sc. vasa), vessels inlaid with gold, Mart. 2, 43, 11; 6, 94, 2; 14, 97, 1.
chryses: A priest of Apollo, from Chryse, in Troas, the father of Astynome, on account of whose close captivity by Agamemnon, Apollo sent a pestilence upon the Grecian hosts, Hyg. Fab. 121; Ov. A. A. 2, 402.—As a title of a tragedy of Pacuvius, Cic. Or. 46, 155; id. Div. 1, 57, 131 al.—Hence, , , , = Χρν   σηίς, his daughter Astynome, Ov. Tr. 2, 373; id. R. Am. 469.
chryseus: Golden: basiliscus,i. e. gold - colored,App. Herb. 128.—Subst.: chrȳsĕa, ōrum, n., golden vessels, Mart. 9, 95, 4.
chrysippus: One of the most distinguished of the Stoic philosophers, from Soli, in Cilicia, a pupil of Cleanthes and Zeno, Cic. Ac. 2, 23, 73; 2, 24, 75; 2, 27, 87 al.; id. de Or. 1, 11, 50; id. Fat. 4, 7; Hor. S. 2, 3, 44; id. Ep. 1, 2, 4; Sen. Ep. 113, 18; Lact. 3, 18, 15; Pers. 6, 80. —Hence
· Chrȳsippēus, a, um, , of Chrysippus, Cic. Ac. 2, 30, 96: sophisma,Hier. Ep. 69, 2.
A physician of Cnidus, in the time of Alexander the Great, Plin. 20, 3, 8, § 17; 20, 10, 43, § 111.—Hence, chrȳ-sippēa, ae, f. (sc. herba), a plant named after him, Plin. 26, 9, 60, § 93.
A freedman of Cicero, Cic. Att. 7, 2, 8 al.
Chrysippus Vettius, an architect, Cic. Fam. 7, 14, 1; id. Att. 13, 29, 2 al.
chrysis: A comic person in Terence and Trabea, Cic. de Or. 2, 80, 327; id. Tusc. 4, 31, 67; Ter. And. 1, 1, 58 al.
chrysites: A precious stone, also called phloginos, Plin. 37, 10, 66, § 179.
chrysitis: Adj., gold-colored: chrysitis spuma. found in silver mines,Plin. 33, 6, 35, § 106.
Subst., a plant, also called chrysocome, q. v., Plin. 21, 8, 26, § 50; 21, 20, 85, § 148.
chrysoaspides: A kind of soldiers under Alexander Severus, Lampr. Alex. Sev. 50.
chrysocalis: A plant, also called parthenium, App. Herb. 23.
chrysocanthos: A kind of ivy which bears gold-colored berries, App. Herb. 119; called in Plin. 16, 34, 62, § 147, , = χρυσόκαρπος.
chrysocolla: A precious stone, called also amphitane, Plin. 37, 10, 54, § 147.
chrysogonus: L. Cornelius, a freedman of Sylla.
A slave of Verres, Cic. Verr. 2, 1, 36, § 92.
A player on the cithara, Juv. 6, 74; Cic. Rosc. Am. 2, 6; cf. id. ib. 43, 124.
chrysographatus: Inlaid with gold: scuta, Val. Imp. ap. Treb. Claud. 14.
chrysolachanum: Garden orach, called also atriplex: Atriplex hortensis, Linn.; Plin. 27, 8, 43, § 66 sq.
chrysolithos: Chrysolite, the topaz of the Greeks and of modern mineralogists, Plin. 37, 9, 42, § 126; Prop. 2 (3), 16, 44; Ov. M. 2, 109; Prud. Psych. 854; Isid. Orig. 16, 15, 2.
chrysomelum: A kind of quince, Plin. 15, 11, 10, § 37.—Hence, chrȳsŏmēlĭnus, a, um, : mala, the same,Col. 5, 10, 19.
chrysopastus: A species of our topaz, Sol. 30 fin.
chrysophrys: A sea-fish with a golden spot over each eye: Sparus aurata, Linn.; Ov. Hal. 111; Plin. 32, 11, 54, § 152.
chrysopis: A precious variety of our topaz, Plin. 37, 10, 56, § 156.
chrysoprasus: The chrysoprase, a precious stone of a golden-yellow and a leek-green color, Plin.  37, 5, 20, § 77; Prud. Psych. 865; Isid. Orig. 16, 7, 7; 16, 14, 8; Ambros. in Psa. 118, Serm. 16, § 41 sq.; also called , Plin. 37, 8, 34, § 113.
chrysopteros: A kind of jasper, Plin. 37, 8, 32, § 109; Ambros. in Psa. 118, Serm. 16, § 41 sq.
chrysorrhoas: The name of several rivers in Coelesyria, in Lydia, in Bithynia, and in Pontus, Plin. 5, 18, 16, § 74; 5, 32, 43, § 148; 5, 29, 30, § 110; 6, 4, 4, § 14.
chrysos: Gold, Plaut. Bacch. 2, 3, 6 (in a pun with the name Chrysalus).
Chrysos melas, black ivy, App. Herb. 98.
chrysothales: A kind of aizoon or houseleek, wall-pepper, called also erithales, trithales, and isoetes, Plin. 25, 13, 102, § 160.
chthonius: One of the Sparti (produced from the teeth of the dragon), Hyg. Fab. 178; Stat. Th. 2, 538.
chuni: Chūni and Chunni, ōrum, v. Hunni
chus: A measure for liquids, = congius, Rhemn. Fann. Pond. 7, 70.
chylisma: The extracted juice of a plant, Scrib. Comp. 23.
chylus: The extracted juice of a plant, Veg. 5, 37 and 65.
chymus: The fluid of the stomach, chyle, Ser. Samm. 48, 900.
chytropus: A pot or chafing-dish with feet for coals, Vulg. Lev. 11, 35.
